blocks.text: 1. GloVe

blocks.alt: A co-occurrence matrix goes through GloVe to produce word vectors

blocks.text: Word2Vec and Skip-gram, already covered, learn purely from local context windows. GloVe, a technique combining ideas from global word co-occurrence statistics, takes a genuinely different, complementary approach.
It genuinely blends local prediction-based learning with genuinely global count-based statistics, a combination explored throughout this topic.

3. Local Context Versus Global Context

blocks.alt: Word2Vec uses a local context window while GloVe uses global co-occurrence

blocks.text: There are two genuinely different sources of training signal available. Word2Vec and Skip-gram, already covered, use only nearby context windows, a genuinely local signal already covered there.
GloVe's own genuinely different approach, explored throughout this topic, is genuinely global instead: genuinely counting co-occurrences across the entire corpus rather than within a small window.

blocks.text: 4. The Co-occurrence Matrix

blocks.alt: Word A and word B produce a co-occurrence count

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely counting co-occurrences across the entire corpus, already covered in this topic. GloVe genuinely builds one giant matrix counting how often every word pair appears together.
This co-occurrence matrix genuinely becomes the entire training signal, replacing individual context windows, a genuinely foundational structure explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Ratios Of Co-occurrence Probabilities
This connects back to the co-occurrence matrix, already covered in this topic. GloVe's own genuinely key insight is that ratios of co-occurrence probabilities encode genuine meaning.

Rather than raw counts alone, already covered, these ratios genuinely distinguish related word pairs from unrelated ones, a genuinely subtle but powerful idea explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 6. Word Vectors From Matrix Factorization

blocks.alt: A co-occurrence matrix goes through matrix factorization to produce word vectors

blocks.text: This connects back to the co-occurrence matrix, already covered in this topic. GloVe genuinely factorizes this matrix into two smaller, dense word vector matrices.
This is a genuinely different training mechanism than Skip-gram's own prediction task, already covered in Skip-gram, even though both genuinely arrive at useful, dense word vectors.
7. GloVe Versus Word2Vec, Directly Compared

blocks.alt: GloVe uses global statistics while Word2Vec uses local prediction

blocks.text: This connects back to Word2Vec and Skip-gram, already covered, learning from local prediction. GloVe genuinely learns from global co-occurrence statistics instead, already covered throughout this topic.
These are two genuinely different training philosophies, both already covered, converging on genuinely similar, useful embeddings despite their genuinely different mechanisms.

blocks.text: 8. Pretrained GloVe Vectors

GloVe's own genuinely practical advantage connects back to the co-occurrence matrix requiring the entire corpus upfront, already covered in this topic. Genuinely widely available pretrained vectors exist, trained once on huge corpora like Wikipedia.

These are directly reusable without retraining, a genuinely common practical entry point already covered throughout this topic, letting teams skip the genuinely expensive corpus-wide counting step entirely.

blocks.alt: Needing global statistical structure points toward GloVe

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely wanting global corpus statistics, already covered in this topic. GloVe, already covered in this topic, directly captures exactly that signal.
This connects back to Skip-gram, already covered, favoring genuinely fine-grained local context instead. Skip-gram, already covered, remains the genuinely better choice for that finer local signal.

blocks.text: 11. Embeddings: Progress Recap

items: GloVe combines local prediction-based ideas with global word co-occurrence statistics.
It builds one giant matrix counting how often every word pair co-occurs across the corpus.
Ratios of co-occurrence probabilities, not raw counts alone, encode the genuine meaning GloVe learns.
Word vectors emerge from factorizing this co-occurrence matrix into two smaller, dense matrices.
This global, count-based mechanism differs from Skip-gram's own local, prediction-based mechanism.
Both approaches converge on similarly useful embeddings despite their different training philosophies.
Widely available pretrained GloVe vectors, trained on huge corpora, are directly reusable without retraining.
GloVe suits tasks wanting global corpus statistics; Skip-gram suits tasks wanting finer local context.
Next up: fastText, an approach extending these ideas down to the level of subword information.
